query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A predictive approach that is calibrated using multi-scale atomistic descriptors—specifically local strain and chemical bonding variations derived from known high-entropy alloys—will accurately identify new HEAs with anomalously low phonon thermal conductivity by capturing the key local chemical fluctuations that enhance phonon scattering.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) with multi-principal element compositions that display significant local strain and bonding variation.
generation.intervention: Application of a learning-based predictive model calibrated on atomistic descriptors (local strain, bonding fluctuations, and electronegativity differences) gathered from a training set of previously characterized HEAs.
generation.conditions: Test the model on candidate HEAs within the compositional space similar to the training data (e.g., alloys with five to seven principal elements showing strong local chemical fluctuations) and under ambient to moderate temperature conditions relevant for thermal insulation applications.
generation.structural_mediator: Local chemical fluctuation induced by variations in atomic mass, strain fields, and chemical bond fluctuations (stemming from differences in electronegativity) that result in increased lattice distortion.
generation.mechanism: The calibrated descriptors capture the extent of local lattice distortions which enhance phonon scattering, thereby reducing phonon thermal conductivity. This effect, when properly modeled, distinguishes candidate HEAs with outperforming thermal-insulation characteristics compared to predictions from conventional models relying solely on average compositional properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: The predictive approach will identify HEA candidates that exhibit at least a 20% lower lattice thermal conductivity than predicted by traditional methods, due to enhanced phonon scattering from localized strain and chemical heterogeneities.
generation.baseline: Current predictive models that use conventional compositional or averaged thermodynamic parameters without detailed multi-scale atomistic calibration.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is expected to hold for HEAs with compositions similar to the training set and with substantial local chemical fluctuations; its applicability may be limited for HEAs outside these compositional regimes or where the descriptors do not capture additional phenomena (e.g., phase separation or non-stoichiometric effects) influencing phonon scattering.
generation.uncertainty: The extent of improvement (quantified as a 20% reduction) is based on limited training data and may vary with different alloy systems; additional data from a broader compositional range is needed to refine the predictive accuracy.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a set of HEA compositions predicted by the model to have low lattice thermal conductivity and a control set predicted by conventional models. Synthesize both sets and measure their phonon thermal conductivity using techniques like time-domain thermoreflectance or laser flash analysis over a consistent temperature range.
measurements: Lattice thermal conductivity values as a function of temperature
Atomic-scale structural characterization (e.g., using atomic-resolution chemical mapping) to confirm the presence of local strain and bonding variations
Comparative analysis of the predicted versus measured thermal conductivity values
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEAs predicted by the calibrated model do not show a statistically significant (≥20%) reduction in lattice thermal conductivity compared to the control group or if the measured local chemical fluctuations do not correlate with the predicted values, then the hypothesis that the multi-scale atomistic descriptor calibration enhances predictive accuracy for low phonon thermal conductivity is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The difference in electronegativity (another intrinsic characteristic of element) affects the local chemical bonding and plays a vital role for the properties of high-entropy materials, such as the strength and ductility of high-entropy alloys (, , ) for engineered applications, the charge redistribution of high-entropy catalysts () for hydrogen evolution reaction, and the electron transport of high-entropy oxides () for lithium-ion battery. Similar to the mass and strain field fluctuations, the electronegativity difference could increase the complexity of chemical bonding between atoms as the chemical bond fluctuation. Therefore, the contribution of electronegativity difference was also included into the Callaway-Debye model for lattice thermal conductivity calculation (Supplementary Text and table S6). We have found that the chemical bond fluctuation (ΓC) demonstrates a noticeable contribution to lattice thermal conductivity in GeTe-AgSbMn compared to other two samples (Fig. 5B), which is derived from the decreased electronegativity difference of Mn (1.55), Pb (2.33), and Sn (1.96) to other constituent elements Ge (2.01), Ag (1.93), Sb (2.05), and Te (2.10).

We applied atomic-resolution chemical mapping for the distribution and fluctuation of elements in high-entropy thermoelectric materials with a variety of elemental combinations. With the fluctuation evaluation of each element, we clearly revealed that the fluctuations of alloying elements were directly related to the discrepancy on atomic mass, radius, and electronegativity of these elements to the matrix elements in high-entropy samples. With the estimation on the respective contributions of the element characteristics, we found that the mass and electronegativity have the comparable contribution to local chemical fluctuation while there is a slight influence from the radius. Moreover, the local chemical fluctuation tailored by altering the constituent elements could reduce the lattice thermal conductivity, in addition to the increased entropy by combining more elements. Large lattice distortion and strain fluctuation were induced by strong elemental fluctuation to largely strengthen phonon scattering for low lattice thermal conductivity.
